name: Referral programme design
summary: Turn the recommendations your work already earns into a habit: when to ask, who on your own list to ask first and for what, what you give back, the words for each ask and the note an introducer forwards, and how every introduction is recorded. You send each message yourself.

sources.title: Its own referrals working guide, and its own record of how that guide was improved on 16 October 2026, item by item, with the source of each idea.

sources.contribution: The referral programme as a loop from the moment of asking to the thanks, asking just after the client has felt the value of the work, a message written in advance so passing it on takes no effort, choosing deliberately what is given back, and counting what the programme produces.

A short note naming the owner, for an introducer to pass on, matching the ask to what the person has seen, the easy no, asking before using the introducer's name with the person they suggest, an introduction offered in return, the thank-you after the introduction, and a single follow-up.
Tracing every line about a person to what the inputs say, in a separate list of where each line comes from, with anything unsupported left as a slot or a proposal to confirm.
Using a client's own recorded words exactly, never a rewording (from its intake questionnaire).

Breaking an output into its separate statements and anchoring each one to its source before anyone acts on it: here, each decision about a person traced to the row and column it rests on, and every quotation checked word for word against its row.
